diagnosis.title: JS Float serialization drops negative zero and violates scalar/FloatArray codec round trips
trace: Test stack points to generated commons.js:161607, whose preceding Float32Array literal is [-0.0, 1.5, NaN, Infinity], corresponding to test source line51.
FloatArrayType maps every element through FloatType.serializeAsValue, then length-frames the resulting strings.

FloatType has no serialization override and inherits AdaptiveNavType<T>.serializeAsValue(value)=value.toString(). The generated generic serializer calls the exported nullable Any.toString wrapper and ultimately the JavaScript number toString.
JavaScript numeric toString renders -0 as "0". Existing Float parseValue compiles to toDouble(value), which uses unary +; parsing "0" gives positive zero.

Float-array equality calls stdlib contentEquals_8/contentEqualsInternal. The generated equals helper accepts NaN pairs and distinguishes signed zeros using reciprocals, so the regression oracle is correct.
diagnosis.impact: The executed FloatArray round trip loses its first element sign; direct FloatType scalar codecs share the same source path. Controller saved FloatArray payloads use this codec, so their signed-zero content is also at risk. No full controller negative-zero reproduction was separately run.
diagnosis.analogous_paths: FloatArrayType is the only float collection codec in AdaptiveNavType. Encoded serialization and parsing delegate FloatType; raw single, incremental and bulk float parsing also delegate FloatType.parseValue and do not require a format rewrite. No Float-list codec or unrelated API needs changing.
diagnosis.proposed_correction: Add a common FloatType.serializeAsValue override: if (value == 0f && value.toBits() == Int.MIN_VALUE) "-0.0" else value.toString(). Do not use value == -0f alone; both signs compare equal. Preserve other values, framing, raw parsing and the existing failed oracle.
proposed_regressions: Explicit scalar negative-zero and positive-zero bit checks before and after round trip; encoded representations must differ.
Explicit FloatArray round trips covering both zero signs, finite values, NaN and both infinities; use bit checks to localize the failure and retain the original primitive-array regression.
Run the original and added cases on JS and desktop; repeat supported Wasm/Native matrix under lead scheduling.

/**
     * The inverse of [serializeAsValue]. Raw [parseValue] deliberately does not
     * URI-decode strings or interpret framed arrays.
     */
    open fun parseSerializedValue(value: String): T = parseValue(value)

/**
     * Serialize a value of this AdaptiveNavType into a String.
     *
     * Scalar built-ins use their canonical text. Strings use UTF-8 percent encoding
     * and distinguish null from the literal "null". Arrays use length-framed
     * elements, with "null" for a null array and "[]" for an empty array.
     * Decode with [parseSerializedValue], not the raw [parseValue] API.
     *
     * This method can be override for custom serialization implementation on types such
     * custom AdaptiveNavType classes.
     *
     * @param value a value representing this AdaptiveNavType to be serialized into a String
     * @return serialized String value of [value]
     */
    open fun serializeAsValue(value: T): String {
        return value.toString()
    }
